question: How much does replacing PVDF with PVDF latex and CMC raise the solids content of NMC 532 slurries, and by what share does the higher solids content cut the primary drying time of the graphite coating?

trace.query: SELECT id, page, text, strength FROM atoms WHERE text ILIKE '%dry%' OR text ILIKE '%solids%' OR text ILIKE '%drying%' ORDER BY page, top
SELECT id, page, text FROM lines WHERE page=8 ORDER BY top

WITH a AS (SELECT CAST(regexp_extract(text,'from (\d+) wt%',1) AS INT) AS s0, CAST(regexp_extract(text,'to (\d+) wt%',1) AS INT) AS s1 FROM atoms WHERE id='p8.L32'),
b AS (SELECT CAST(regexp_extract(t.text,'from (\d+)',1) AS INT) AS t0 FROM atoms t WHERE t.id='p8.L34'),
c AS (SELECT CAST(regexp_extract(text,'s to (\d+) s',1) AS INT) AS t1 FROM atoms WHERE id='p8.L35')
SELECT a.s1 - a.s0 AS solids_gain_points, b.t0 - c.t1 AS drying_time_cut_s, (b.t0 - c.t1) * 100.0 / b.t0 AS drying_cut_pct FROM a, b, c

rendered: Replacing the PVDF binder with PVDF latex and CMC raises the solids content of the NMC 532[1] slurry from 45 wt% to 65 wt%[2], a gain of 20[3] percentage points, and the document says this is achieved without increasing the slurry viscosity[4]. The higher solids content shortens the primary drying time of the graphite coating from 51[5] s to 34 s for a graphite coating with a loading of 10 mg/cm^2[6]. That is a cut of 17[7] seconds, which is 3,333%[8] of the original primary drying time, or about a third.
